cases.name: hush-file-write
cases.doc: RESOLVED (was a known divergence): under -q (*hush* = true), `pr` to a FILE stream now WRITES on every impl. *hush* only gates stdout, never stderr or an explicit file stream. Driven as `{bin} eval -q -l PROG`. S42 shen-c/shen-forth need host `pr` overrides (stock writer.kl returns without writing whenever *hush* for every stream) and eval -q/-l. Previously shen-lua/shen-rust SILENCED the write (zero-byte file) under -q while shen-cl/shen-go/ShenScript wrote. Hard agreement: every available impl must land in the same bucket (all 'written'); any impl that silences the write is a real FAIL. UPSTREAM shen-scheme 0.50 (tizoc release) uses stock writer.kl, so `-q` SILENCES the file write there (zero bytes) and it FAILS this case by design; the pyrex41 fork reapplies the stdout-only *hush* override on top of 0.50 (pyrex41/shen-scheme#9).

cases.name: load-toplevel-echo
cases.doc: RESOLVED (was a known divergence): `(load FILE)` now echoes each toplevel form's evaluated value on every impl, cache state notwithstanding. The canonical kernel load (klambda/load.kl -> shen.eval-and-print) PRINTS each toplevel result before returning `loaded` (the echo from `shen eval -l FILE` / `(load FILE)` at the REPL; NOT `script` mode, which is quiet everywhere -- so this case uses eval mode). shen-rust and shen-go always emitted it; shen-lua emitted it on a COLD fasl cache but DROPPED it on a WARM fasl-cache HIT (boot.lua returned `loaded` straight out of fasl_replay without re-running the kernel load), making `(load file)` stdout cache-state dependent -- a cross-port divergence AND an intra-port nondeterminism. Fixed in shen-lua by recording the per-form echo bytes as fasl "e" records on the miss and re-pr'ing them on the hit (pyrex41/shen-lua#40, PR #41). The cosmetic `run time:` banner stays dropped on a warm hit by design; the normaliser strips the whole banner (text line + the blank line its leading newline produces; that blank-line drop was documented but missing until the 42.2 move, which left this case tagged as a known divergence) so that omission is not itself a divergence. Now asserted as a HARD agreement: every available impl must echo `"PROBE"` / `42` / `(fn p)` (the last stripped by the normaliser) then `loaded`; any impl that drops the value echo is a real FAIL.

cases.name: bigint-2pow53-plus-1
cases.doc: DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE (Shen leaves number precision to the platform). 2^53+1 is the first integer an IEEE double cannot hold. Ports with exact integers here print 9007199254740993: bignums (shen-cl on SBCL/ECL, shen-erl, shen-scheme) and 64-bit integers (shen-julia, shen-c, shen-rust, shen-swift, shen-truffle). Ports whose only number is a double (shen-go, ShenScript, shen-lua) print 9007199254740992. The table pins each port to its bucket: reported as DIVERGE, but a port that changes bucket FAILS.

cases.name: bigint-2pow63-ordered
cases.doc: DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE (Shen leaves number precision to the platform). Bignum ports shen-cl/shen-erl/shen-scheme return true. Shen-C v0.3.0 raises a catchable signed-64-bit overflow error, pinned here to Integer overflow. Shen-julia wraps and returns false; shen-rust/shen-swift/shen-truffle promote to a rounded double and return false; shen-go/ShenScript/shen-lua use doubles and return false. The handler exposes the exact error text, so an unrelated error does not match the documented bucket.
